scope: One full authorized R4 guide plus one Original C transfer; no segmentation, processing, retry or canonical edit
text:
It’s hard to leave an app alone when it looks like something you could sell.

I’ve gotta get better at that. With AI, I can get something looking pretty good before I’ve worked out why anyone would actually use it.

So I’m building this GTM Engine to help me work through that. It looks at the code, then researches who might use it and what they’re doing already. Because if they’ve already got a way that works, why would they bother with mine?

But I still wanna let someone try it on something they actually need to do. Do they choose mine, or go back to what they were using before?

Maybe I’ve gotta build a bit more to find that out. That’s fine. But I’ve got other projects I wanna work on too, so I want more to go on than how good this one looks.

And if I just enjoy using it myself, I can leave it at that. It’s okay to have a hobby.

So you guys tell me, what made you decide to turn something you’d built into a business?

The line about a hobby has light, faintly amused acceptance, without an added laugh or an announcer punchline. End by asking people a real question, casually open and interested, with the final word fully spoken and a brief natural quiet ending. Keep pauses proportionate to the thought: short within clauses, slightly longer at real turns, with no dramatic silence after every line. Do not sound like a narrator, presenter, commercial, motivational speech or polished radio read. No sing-song phrasing, theatrical voice, imitation of someone else, fake stumbles, fillers, added breaths for effect, laughter, ambience, effects or music. Do not speak these directions.
